added_meaning: Senate 100051(5) fingerprint and DNA purposes are within the additional $2,055,000,000 fiscal year 2025 Secretary of Homeland Security account through September 30, 2029. Both purposes share the printed circumstance of aliens and alien children entering the United States without a valid visa. Subparagraph (A) funds collecting fingerprints, in accordance with section 262 and subsections (a)(3) and (b) of section 235 of the Immigration and Nationality Act. Subparagraph (B) separately funds collecting DNA, in accordance with sections 235(d) and 287(b) of that Act. These are funding purposes with their own incorporated authorities, not a determination that every alien or child is subject to every collection power or that funded collection actually occurred. Captured 262(a) concerns an alien now or hereafter in the United States who is fourteen years of age or older, has not been registered and fingerprinted under section 1201(b) or section 30 or 31 of the Alien Registration Act, 1940, and remains in the United States for thirty days or longer. All those conditions are common to its duty to apply for registration and to be fingerprinted before the expiration of such thirty days. Captured 262(b) separately requires a parent or legal guardian to apply for registration of an alien now or hereafter in the United States who is less than fourteen years of age, has not been registered under those named provisions, and remains in the United States for thirty days or longer, before that period expires. That parent/guardian provision prints registration, not the same under-14 fingerprint duty. Whenever an alien attains his fourteenth birthday in the United States, the separate rule requires in-person registration and fingerprinting within thirty days thereafter. Captured 262(c) retains the Attorney General's discretionary nonimmigrant fingerprint waiver on the basis of reciprocity pursuant to prescribed regulations; no actual waiver is inferred. Complete 235(a)(3) concerns inspection of aliens, including crewmen, who apply for or otherwise seek admission, readmission or transit; it does not itself print a fingerprint command. Complete material 235(b)(1)/(2) screening, exceptions, asylum/fear/interview/review/consultation/detention and contiguous-return conditions remain bound, together with the original favorable-admission challenge. January 29, 2025 Public Law 119-1 renumbers that original challenge from (3) to (4) and inserts the distinct State enforcement (3); the captured 2024 wording is not relabeled as an unamended 2025 subsection. Complete 235(d) retains its own belief-based conveyance search, detention/delivery with the alien-crewmember exception, named oath/evidence powers and subpoena-purpose/court-enforcement conditions. Complete 287(b) retains the designated officer/employee oath/evidence scope and its own knowing-or-willful false-evidence/perjury conditions. Neither cited provision expressly names DNA collection. That literal observation does not resolve whether other law, implementation rules or this funding language supports a proposed collection; question 50 reserves the exact DNA authority/application interaction. Question 51 separately reserves the fingerprint-purpose no-valid-visa circumstance alongside the incorporated registration age/prior-registration/duration/waiver paths and inspection procedures. No statutory repeal, guaranteed discretion outcome, universal biometric collection or actual child/parent/status/registration finding is inferred.
